newsitem.title: UK: UK beet crop benefits from rain, still needs more.
newsitem.headline: UK beet crop benefits from rain, still needs more.

text.p: Britain's 1997/98 sugar beet crop could still benefit from more rains despite last weekend's wet weather in parched growing areas, beet experts said on Tuesday.
Some 18 millimetres of rain fell on south-eastern England between April 25 and 27, continuing into April 28, but the moisture was still not enough to replenish ground water supplies, they said.
"It was very welcome and we're looking forward to a pattern of rain and sunshine for the rest of the summer," said a spokesman for British Sugar.
"But we could have done with several days of gentle soaking rain," he said, adding that underlying soils were still dry.
Farming sources in East Anglia, Britain's main beet area, said windy conditions had minimised the rain's beneficial effects by drying out soil and crops quickly.
But many crops were developing well despite the dry weather although there some concern about cold night temperatures as beet needs a warm seed bed to germinate.
"People are very surprised how well things like sugar beet have germinated, given how dry the soil is," said one source.
Before last week's rain, farmers had reported weed growth and the destruction of beets by mice in dry seed beds, causing one west Midlands crop to be re-drilled.

Beet experts said patchy emergence would be another problem as bed conditions have varied during the drilling programme -- but the recent rains would have helped to balance out the different stages of development.

"Most of the crop is emerging reasonably well and for that which went into very dry seedbeds, it (the rain) will certainly have helped," said Simon Kerr of the National Institute of Agricultural Botany.
"There were some weed problems...but that should even itself out as once you've got a reasonable plant then they (beets) are fairly secure," he said.
Independent forecaster WSC said western Europe was trending drier again, adding that Britain would see dry and mild weather from May 1 to 3.
In its forecast to dawn on April 30, Britain's Meteorological Office said most places would be dry and warm with sunny spells, although some frost could be seen in northern areas.
